en.greeting: Hi! Today is all about listening: letters, numbers, greetings and classroom instructions. Play each sound as many times as you like.

steps.title: Letters you'll hear
steps.text: When people spell a name, they use English letter names. Tap each letter to hear it.
steps.body: English letters have their own names, not the Indonesian ones: Indonesian says E 'e' and I 'i', English says **E** 'ee' and **I** 'eye'. Listen for the pairs that sound alike to Indonesian ears: **A** ('ay') and **R** ('ar'), **E** ('ee') and **I** ('eye'), **G** ('jee') and **J** ('jay'). **W** is 'double-you' (it looks like two U's) and **Y** is 'why'. **Z** is 'zed' in British English, 'zee' in American English. **Double** means two of the same letter: 'A, double N, A' is Anna.

steps.title: Listen: spell the name
steps.text: Press play. Listen to each letter, especially the second one.

question.prompt: Listen. How is the name spelled?
question.explanation: You heard R-**E**-Z-A: the second letter is 'ee', which is **E** (I is 'eye'). The third letter is 'zed' (American English says 'zee'), so it's Z, not S ('es').

steps.title: Numbers you'll hear
steps.text: Numbers are where listening gets tricky. Tap each one and listen to the **stress**: the part of the word said louder and longer (written in capitals here).
steps.body: For **13–19** the stress is at the **end** (thir**TEEN**); for **30, 40, 50…** it is at the **start** (**THIR**ty). Phone numbers come **one digit at a time**, often with **oh** for 0 (it looks like the letter O) and **double** for two of the same. Prices: *twenty thousand rupiah* = Rp20.000. After a number, **thousand** has no -s, even for many thousands: not 'twenty thousands'.

steps.title: Listen: how much?
steps.text: Listen for the stress: at the start or at the end?

question.listen: The coffee is thirty thousand rupiah.
question.prompt: Listen. How much is the coffee?
question.explanation: You heard **THIRty thousand**, with the stress at the start: Rp30.000. Thirteen has the stress at the end (thir**TEEN**), and three is one short beat.

steps.title: Listen: the phone number
steps.text: Listen in small groups of digits. Play it again if you need to.

question.prompt: Listen. Which phone number do you hear?
question.explanation: The number is **0857 1190 3324**. The other two swap two digits — a very common listening slip, so check each group of four.

steps.title: Greetings you'll hear
steps.text: Now let's listen to people saying hello and goodbye.
steps.body: **Good morning / afternoon / evening** are for meeting people. **Good night** means goodbye at night, not hello. So Indonesian *selamat malam* has two English versions: **Good evening** when you arrive, **Good night** when you leave. To **How are you?** you answer **I'm fine, thanks. And you?** To **Nice to meet you** you answer **Nice to meet you too.**

steps.title: Listen and reply
steps.text: Listen to what the person says, then choose your answer.

question.listen: Hi, I'm Dewi. Nice to meet you.
question.prompt: Listen. What is a good reply?
question.explanation: Dewi said **Nice to meet you**, so you answer **Nice to meet you too.** 'I'm fine, thanks' answers How are you?, and Good night is for leaving.

steps.title: Classroom instructions
steps.text: Last group: what teachers say in class.
steps.body: Instructions start with the **action word**: *listen, repeat, open, close, sit, stand, write, look*. Catch the first word and you know what to do. Watch the opposites: **open ↔ close**, **sit down ↔ stand up**. **please** (tolong, silakan) can come at the start or at the end; it just makes it polite.

steps.title: Listen: what do you do?
steps.text: Two actions this time. Listen for both.

question.listen: Close your books and listen, please.
question.prompt: Listen to the teacher. What do you do?
question.explanation: The teacher said **Close** your books and **listen**. Open is the opposite of close, and nobody asked you to write.

steps.title: Quick review
steps.text: Flip each card. Try to hear the sound in your head first.

steps.title: Cheat sheet
steps.text: What you hear and what it means, on one page.

artifact.title: Cheat sheet · First listening
artifact.intro: Letters, numbers, greetings and instructions you'll hear, and what they mean.
tips: Listen for **key words** (a name, a number, an action), not every word.
Stress at the **end** = 13–19; stress at the **start** = 30, 40, 50…
Didn't catch it? Say **Sorry? Can you repeat that, please?**

id.greeting: Hai! Hari ini semuanya tentang menyimak: huruf, angka, salam dan instruksi kelas. Putar setiap suara sesering yang kamu mau.

steps.title: Huruf yang akan kamu dengar
steps.text: Saat orang mengeja nama, mereka memakai nama huruf versi Inggris. Ketuk setiap huruf untuk mendengarnya.
steps.body: Nama huruf bahasa Inggris berbeda dari bahasa Indonesia: kita bilang E 'e' dan I 'i', bahasa Inggris bilang **E** 'ii' dan **I** 'ai'. Dengarkan pasangan yang terdengar mirip: **A** ('ay', dibaca ei) dan **R** ('ar'), **E** ('ee', dibaca ii) dan **I** ('eye', dibaca ai), **G** ('jee', dibaca ji) dan **J** ('jay', dibaca jei). **W** dibaca 'double-you' (bentuknya seperti dua U) dan **Y** dibaca 'why'. **Z** dibaca 'zed' (UK) atau 'zi' (Amerika). **Double** berarti dua huruf yang sama: 'A, double N, A' adalah Anna.

steps.title: Dengar: eja namanya
steps.text: Tekan play. Dengarkan setiap huruf, terutama huruf kedua.

question.explanation: Kamu mendengar R-**E**-Z-A: huruf kedua dibaca 'ee' (ii), yaitu **E** (I dibaca 'eye', ai). Huruf ketiga dibaca 'zed' (orang Amerika bilang 'zi'), jadi Z, bukan S ('es').

steps.title: Angka yang akan kamu dengar
steps.text: Di angka, menyimak jadi lebih menantang. Ketuk satu per satu dan dengarkan **tekanannya**: bagian kata yang diucapkan lebih keras dan lebih panjang (di sini ditulis dengan huruf besar).
steps.body: Untuk **13–19** tekanannya di **akhir** (thir**TEEN**); untuk **30, 40, 50…** tekanannya di **awal** (**THIR**ty). Nomor telepon diucapkan **satu angka demi satu angka**, sering dengan **oh** untuk 0 (bentuknya seperti huruf O) dan **double** untuk dua angka sama. Harga: *twenty thousand rupiah* = Rp20.000. Setelah angka, **thousand** tidak pakai -s, walaupun ribuan: bukan 'twenty thousands'.

steps.title: Dengar: berapa harganya?
steps.text: Dengarkan tekanannya: di awal atau di akhir?

question.listen: The coffee is thirty thousand rupiah.
question.explanation: Kamu mendengar **THIRty thousand**, dengan tekanan di awal: Rp30.000. Thirteen tekanannya di akhir (thir**TEEN**), dan three hanya satu ketukan pendek.

steps.title: Dengar: nomor teleponnya
steps.text: Dengarkan per kelompok angka. Putar lagi kalau perlu.

question.prompt: Dengarkan. Nomor telepon mana yang kamu dengar?
question.explanation: Nomornya **0857 1190 3324**. Dua pilihan lain menukar dua angka — kesalahan menyimak yang sangat umum, jadi cek setiap kelompok empat angka.

steps.title: Salam yang akan kamu dengar
steps.text: Sekarang kita dengarkan orang menyapa dan berpamitan.
steps.body: **Good morning / afternoon / evening** dipakai saat bertemu. **Good night** artinya pamit di malam hari, bukan menyapa. Jadi *selamat malam* punya dua versi dalam bahasa Inggris: **Good evening** saat datang, **Good night** saat pamit. Untuk **How are you?** jawab **I'm fine, thanks. And you?** Untuk **Nice to meet you** jawab **Nice to meet you too.**

steps.title: Dengar dan balas
steps.text: Dengarkan apa yang diucapkan, lalu pilih jawabanmu.

question.listen: Hi, I'm Dewi. Nice to meet you.
question.explanation: Dewi bilang **Nice to meet you**, jadi kamu jawab **Nice to meet you too.** 'I'm fine, thanks' menjawab How are you?, dan Good night untuk berpamitan.

steps.title: Instruksi di kelas
steps.text: Kelompok terakhir: yang diucapkan guru di kelas.
steps.body: Instruksi diawali **kata tindakan**: *listen, repeat, open, close, sit, stand, write, look*. Tangkap kata pertamanya dan kamu tahu apa yang harus dilakukan. Perhatikan pasangan berlawanan: **open ↔ close**, **sit down ↔ stand up**. **please** (tolong, silakan) bisa di awal atau di akhir; fungsinya supaya sopan.

steps.title: Dengar: apa yang kamu lakukan?
steps.text: Kali ini ada dua tindakan. Dengarkan keduanya.

question.listen: Close your books and listen, please.
question.prompt: Dengarkan gurunya. Apa yang kamu lakukan?
question.explanation: Guru bilang **Close** your books dan **listen**. Open kebalikan dari close, dan tidak ada yang menyuruhmu menulis.

steps.title: Ulasan cepat
steps.text: Balik setiap kartu. Coba bayangkan bunyinya dulu di kepalamu.

steps.title: Contekan
steps.text: Apa yang kamu dengar dan artinya, dalam satu halaman.

artifact.title: Contekan · Menyimak pertama
artifact.intro: Huruf, angka, salam dan instruksi yang akan kamu dengar, beserta artinya.
tips: Dengarkan **kata kunci** (nama, angka, tindakan), bukan setiap kata.
Tidak tertangkap? Bilang **Sorry? Can you repeat that, please?**
